page: The Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-amd is a High Performance virtual server configured with 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC cores on the x86_64 architecture. Operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, this instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with 180 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate compute capabilities alongside significant memory bandwidth bottlenecks. The server achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 1641.0 and a multi-core score of 5232.0, placing its raw processing power in the average tier. However, while cached small-block memory reads reached 355.85 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write speeds fell into the bottom 10% of tested systems at 17.9 GB/sec and 12.56 GB/sec respectively. Similarly, Passmark database operations and static web serving throughput registered in the lower percentiles.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high ratio of local NVMe storage relative to its shared compute resources, making it a viable option for storage-centric workloads that do not require sustained, high-throughput memory access. The shared CPU allocation introduces potential resource contention, which is reflected in the weaker Passmark CPU physics and extended instruction scores.

This server configuration is best suited for lightweight, non-memory-intensive workloads. Appropriate use cases include basic software compilation, text processing, and development environments. It is not recommended for high-throughput database hosting, intensive web serving, or large-scale LLM inference due to its constrained memory bandwidth and shared CPU architecture.
